title: NIC interrupt affinity & PTP clock jitter — multi-GPU scheduling scratchpad
content:
Quick note: this is a scratchpad capturing the odd interactions we saw between NIC interrupt handling, PTP time sync adjustments, and NCCL progress stalls during multi-GPU pipeline/tensor-parallel inference. Trying to collect reproducible configs and a short experiment plan so we can either rule this out as infra/driver noise or pin a mitigatable cause.

Context / why this surfaced
- During a late-night load test of the 32B pipelined split (2-node, 8xA100/node), we saw intermittent 0.5–5ms tail spikes ~every 30–90s affecting end-to-end token latency. Not correlated with CPU steal or obvious host CPU load.
- Concurrently, a couple of runs logged NCCL WARN about "operation progress delayed" with timestamps matching the spikes.
- Hypothesis: asynchronous NIC activity (interrupts / Rx ring processing), combined with small PTP clock adjustments on host NICs, intermittently preempt the CPU threads that NCCL relies on for progress (esp. for cross-node rendezvous).

Background notes and prior art
- We know NCCL progress relies on timely polling by host CPU threads when using Infiniband/GPUDirect RDMA (and even with TCP fallback).
- Interrupt handling, irqbalance, and kernel PTP adjustments can migrate work across cores and cause momentary context switches that break low-latency polling assumptions.
- Similar symptoms reported in infra Slack (see linked thread) and a handful of external posts about RDMA + PTP causing micro-pauses.

Hardware / software baseline used for repro
- 2 x nodes (baremetal staging): H12 + 8xA100-40GB (PCIe), Mellanox HDR100 IB, kernel 6.1.12, OFED 5.13.1, CUDA 12.1, NCCL 2.18.3
- NICs: ConnectX-6 Dx, PTP enabled for ML infra time sync via internal NTP/PTP mesh
- Scheduler: serving-runtime v0.49 release candidate harness (custom per-request pipeline placement script)
- Test harness: our synthetic-chat generator with 512 token contexts, T=0.0 greedy, 8 concurrent clients per node, constant qps to saturate streaming path
- Baseline config: irqbalance enabled, net.core.netdev_max_backlog default, nohz_full not set, rq-affinity default

What I instrumented quickly (commands run)
- dmesg | grep -i nccl
- sar -q / mpstat -P ALL during run
- trace-cmd record -e irq:* -e sched:sched_switch -F 500 -o irq.trace (light)
- ethtool -S mlx5_core | egrep "rx|tx|ptp|irq"
- git hash of runtime and a copy of the exact launch script
- tcpdump -i ib0 -w ib-repro.pcap (spike windows)
- perf record -a -e cycles,instructions,context-switches -F 99 -- sleep 300  (samples aligned to spike windows)

Observed signals and log snippets (initial pass)
- At t=00:02:13.84 we saw a 1.8ms latency spike. trace-cmd shows a burst of softirq/IRQ handling on core 3 for ~900us, immediately followed by a PTP adj event (kernel: "phc adj" entries).
- NCCL log snippet: "[rank 1] WARN operation progress delayed 1839 us" – aligns to the same timestamp window.
- perf flamegraphs show a sudden shift from user-space polling loops into ksoftirqd and then into ptp_clock_adj code paths.
- tcpdump from ib0 shows no lost/late packets, but small burst of retransmissions ~50ms after the spike (maybe consequence, not cause).

Hypotheses (ranked)
1) PTP disciplining (phc/ptp daemon) performs periodic small slews/adjtime that cause irq context shifts and preempt tight polling loops; during these adj events, NIC interrupts get handled on different cores, poll threads get starved -> NCCL progress stalls.
2) irqbalance or netdev RSS moves IRQ affinity dynamically, causing polling threads to miss deadlines; combined with high IRQ rates during inference (large number of small packets), leads to tail spikes.
3) NIC offloads (RSS, RPS) interact poorly with our userland poll strategy; under certain packet timing the kernel toggles processing mode.
4) Rare: NIC firmware bug that does micro-PAUSEs while updating timestamp queues when PTP is active.

Quick experiments to differentiate (what I ran / next runs)
- Disable irqbalance and pin NIC interrupts to dedicated cores (irq affinity) + pin NCCL/poll threads to other isolated cores (use taskset / cset) -> preliminary: spike frequency dropped by ~60% in one run.
- Force PTP off (disable phc2sys) -> spikes dropped to near-zero in short test (2 runs). This strongly implicates PTP adjustments.
- With PTP on, tried nohz_full on cores pinned to NCCL polling. Mixed results; some spikes persist but magnitude shrinks.
- Toggle GPUDirect RDMA off (use TCP fallback) -> spikes still visible but slightly lower magnitude; suggests cross-node RDMA path amplifies sensitivity.

Commands / configs used for repro (notes to replicate)
- echo 0 > /proc/sys/kernel/irq_balance (we used irqbalance service stop and write 0)
- for i in $(ls /proc/irq | grep mlx5); do echo 4 > /proc/irq/$i/smp_affinity; done  # pin to core 2
- taskset -c 3,5 ./launch-infer-harness.sh --pp=8 --tp=4 --clients=8
- systemctl stop phc2sys.service; /etc/init.d/ptp4l stop

Data artifacts saved
- perf data: /tmp/repro/perf-2024-11-18.data
- trace-cmd: /tmp/repro/irq.trace
- pcap: /tmp/repro/ib-repro-2024-11-18.pcap
- short run logs: s3://redwood-staging/repro/nic-ptp-spike-20241118/

Preliminary conclusions (for the notebook)
- PTP-related clock adjustments correlate strongly with stalls. Cutting PTP out of the loop removed most of the spikes in limited runs.
- IRQ placement matters; explicit pinning reduces frequency of spikes. Suggests that migration of interrupt handling across cores can transiently preempt polling threads.
- RDMA path increases the sensitivity/impact (larger stalls when GPUDirect RDMA enabled), possibly because RDMA completion handling interacts with host-side progress requirements.

Open questions / follow-ups
- Can we retrofit the runtime's progress model to be more resilient to short preemption windows? e.g., add watchdog-driven forced-kick for NCCL progress if polling hasn't advanced in X us. Potential risk: noisy/expensive.
- Should infra disable PTP for serving clusters, or limit its aggressiveness? Tradeoffs with time sync for logs and metrics.
- Investigate NIC firmware / driver PTP implementation: are timestamp queue operations synchronous and do they take an unusually long time? (liaise with infra + Mellanox driver team)
- Test on HDR200/400 and with different OFED builds to see if behavior is driver/firmware-specific.
- Try kernel parameter experiments: irqpoll, rcu_nocbs, isolcpus, nohz_full, net.core.busy_poll, netdev_max_backlog tuning. Document perf delta for each.

Proposed next experiment matrix (small, focused)
1) Baseline: irqbalance on, PTP on, RDMA on (10 runs)
2) PTP off, irqbalance on, RDMA on (10 runs)
3) PTP on, irqbalance off + IRQ pinning + isolcpus for poll threads (10 runs)
4) PTP on, RDMA off (TCP), measure stalls (10 runs)
5) Kernel builds: stock 6.1.12 vs 6.3.x backports (small sample)
Metrics to gather: p50/p95/p99 token latency, NCCL WARN counts, ksoftirqd CPU time, number of IRQ migrations (trace-cmd), perf context-switch counts, ib retrans/seq drops.

Notes for run owners / playbook
- Owner: Asha for experiment orchestration; ask infra (Lena) to schedule nodes with different OFED/fw; ask Miguel to collect driver and firmware dumps.
- Do not run on prod clusters; repro needs isolated baremetal.
- Keep wall time per run ~5 minutes and capture 3–4 spikes per run to have statistical power.

Random ideas (future hardening)
- Fast-path: a lightweight watchdog in the runtime that triggers a local "progress poke" to NCCL if no token produced for X us (X in [200, 800]us) — careful: must be bounded CPU cost.
- Encourage infra to avoid aggressive PTP slewing in serving clusters; prefer discipline via NTP/PTPd config that uses slews only off-line and avoids host-side 1ms corrections.
- Consider moving NIC RX handling to cores that are fully isolated away from poll threads; or conversely, co-locate NIC interrupts with poll threads depending on data.

Appendix: quick grep of interesting trace lines
- [2024-11-18 00:02:13.843] ksoftirqd/3: handling mlx5 irq 23 (duration 912us)
- [2024-11-18 00:02:13.951] ptp4l[1123]: phc adj by 350 ns (slew)
- [2024-11-18 00:02:13.960] nccl WARN rank=1 op progress delayed 1839 us

Action items (short)
- [ ] Run experiment matrix above and collect artifacts (Asha)
- [ ] Ask infra to reproduce on a different OFED fw (Lena)
- [ ] Raise a kernel/driver ticket if PTP code path shows long synchronous work (Miguel)
- [ ] Draft runtime watchdog proposal (Jon)

Notes-to-self: keep this doc informal; will migrate a cleaned summary to Confluence (link to come) if we find a root cause.

-- Asha
